## Problem

The lab starts from zero. A working Kailash OS system is the goal.
The release ships bootable images in two formats per profile: a QEMU
disk image (the primary shape) and a bootable ISO. The release
publishes the images as release assets on a signed tag. The task:
download an artefact and state it is exactly what the project built.
Checksums, build provenance and the signed tag must all agree — before
anything boots.

## Solution

Pick the target from the declared matrix. Download from the tagged
release. Then run the three-step verification chain:

```bash
# 1. Download the artefact for your target from the tagged release
#    (e.g. the first release, 2026.01-alpha.1):
#      kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
#    Above-cap artefacts ship split: <…>.part-000 (each chunk ≤1900 MiB)
#    plus a per-part sheet per chunk.

# 2. If chunked, reassemble — then run the whole-file check (the identity check):
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-parts-kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
cat kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2.part-* > \
    kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 3. Verify build provenance + the signed tag:
gh attestation verify kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2 \
    -R kailash-os/kailash-os
git tag -v 2026.01-alpha.1
```

What success looks like:

- the whole-file `sha256sum -c` against `SHA256SUMS` reports OK for
  the download — the release sheet is THE authority on artefact
  identity
- `gh attestation verify` confirms SLSA v1.0 build provenance (plus
  the SPDX SBOM). The provenance builds over the repo's OIDC identity.
  The check holds even after a chunk reassembly. The `cat` step is
  byte-exact, so the attested subject is preserved
- `git tag -v` shows a good GPG signature on the release tag
- the qcow2 boots in any UEFI-capable hypervisor (a choice of
  QEMU/KVM, virt-manager, UTM on Apple Silicon). The ISO boots the
  same profile from optical/USB media

Every artefact is alternatively buildable from the release closure:

```bash
nix build github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-alpha.1#kailash-images-qemu-full
```

## Discussion

- **Which profile:** `minimal` boots the CORE substrate with no tool
  categories. `redteam-ai` is the AI red-team lab scope. `full` is
  the complete live catalogue. `headless-agent` is base + CLI with no
  desktop. The image name encodes the profile — see
  [First profile and first run](first-profile.html) for the
  profile table. The construction enforces the size budgets
  (≤1.5/4/8/10 GB by target). Heavy corpora live in opt-in
  `kailash-data.*` packs, not in the default images — see
  [Refresh wordlists and data packs](../admin/data-packs.html).
- **Chunked assets are packaging, not fragility:** byte-exact split
  parts + per-part sheets on the same release answer the 2 GiB legacy
  asset cap. `cat` reproduces the original bits. The attestation
  verifies the whole file after reassembly.
- **Aarch64 rows exist:** the x86_64 targets use hosted builds. The
  aarch64 (Apple Silicon native) rows build via the project's
  `tools/build-arm-images.sh` — see the images chapter for the
  build-from-tag procedure.
- **Trust chain summary:** signed tag → SLSA provenance + SBOM per
  artefact → SHA256SUMS as the whole-file identity. Do not boot a
  download that fails any link of that chain. Re-download, or build
  from the tag.
